summary.en: Distinguish a table of addresses from a pointer to a fixed-width array, and track jagged row lengths.
summary.bn: অ্যাড্রেসের টেবিল আর নির্দিষ্ট সারির অ্যারের পয়েন্টার আলাদা করো, আর অসমান সারির দৈর্ঘ্য রাখো।

notes: Both declaration forms are available throughout standard C. The examples use C17 and C99-style loops. No newer standard makes a row-pointer type equivalent to a table-of-pointers type merely because their access expressions use similar brackets.

examples.title: A table can reorder selected variables
examples.explanationHtml: The second table entry points at a. Writing through it changes a without changing the entry ordering.

examples.title: A pointer to a row preserves its width
examples.explanationHtml: Advancing row skips one complete three-int row and reaches values four through six.

examples.title: Jagged string lengths
examples.explanationHtml: Each entry selects its own terminated string. The visible lengths differ even though pointer entry types match.

examples.title: Jagged numeric rows
examples.explanationHtml: The separate lengths prevent the second row from being traversed as though it contained two elements.

examples.title: Uninitialized table entries are not rows
examples.explanationHtml: The result is undefined: the second entry has no initialized pointer value. Initialize every entry and check optional null rows.

practice.title: Read a chosen indirect slot
practice.statementHtml: Read index 0 to 2. Print Slot: then the selected target from a pointer table selecting {30,10,20} in that order.
hints: The table order need not match variable declaration order.

practice.title: Print a selected fixed-width row
practice.statementHtml: Read row 0 or 1. Print Matrix row: then the corresponding row of {{1,2,3},{4,5,6}} using a pointer-to-array declaration.
hints: Parentheses bind the pointer before the row brackets.

practice.title: Find a longest jagged literal
practice.statementHtml: Read index 0 to 2. Print Starting entry: then print the longest string among that index and later entries in {"A","Campus","Lab"}; choose the first tie.

practice.title: Sum a bounded jagged selection
practice.statementHtml: Read row 0 or 1 and a prefix count from 0 to its length. Print Jagged row and count: then sum that prefix from rows {2,4} and {6}. Use a pointer table and length table.
hints: Validate the row before indexing its length entry.

quiz.explanation: Brackets bind to rows before the unparenthesized star.

options: A pointer to an array of three ints
quiz.explanation: Parentheses make the star apply before the array suffix.

quiz.prompt: How far does row+1 move for int (*row)[3]?
quiz.explanation: The target type is an array of three ints.

quiz.prompt: What bound is needed for each numeric jagged row?
quiz.explanation: Different targets can hold different numbers of elements.

quiz.prompt: Can swapping pointer-table entries move local target objects in memory?
quiz.explanation: The table stores addresses; exchanging those values changes selection order.

quiz.prompt: What qualification protects literal text in a pointer table?
quiz.explanation: const on char prevents writes through the entries; const on pointer alone would not.

quiz.prompt: Does a non-null row entry guarantee that its old local target still exists?
options: Only if it was once valid
quiz.explanation: A table entry cannot extend target lifetime.

quiz.prompt: Which target values are printed after writing through items[1]?
quiz.explanation: That entry selects a rather than b.

quiz.prompt: What first and last values belong to the advanced fixed-width row pointer?
quiz.explanation: The row stride retains three int elements.

quiz.prompt: What lengths accompany the three jagged literal strings?
quiz.explanation: Each target has an independent terminator position.

examQuestions.question: Contrast int *rows[3] and int (*row)[3] with a storage diagram and explain their stepping.
examQuestions.answerHtml: rows owns three pointer objects; each may select independent int storage with a separately recorded length. The expression rows+1 advances to the next pointer entry. row is one pointer object selecting a complete three-int array; row+1 skips that whole row within a suitable matrix. Neither form may be substituted for the other by casting.

A:1
Campus:6
Lab:3

Each target has an independent terminator position.

examQuestions.question: Read row 0 or 1 and a prefix count from 0 to its length. Print Jagged row and count: then sum that prefix from rows {2,4} and {6}. Use a pointer table and length table.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int a[] = {2, 4}, b[] = {6};
    int *rows[] = {a, b};
    size_t lengths[] = {2, 1};
    int row;
    size_t count;
    puts("Jagged row and count:");
    if (scanf("%d %zu", &row, &count) != 2 || row < 0 || row > 1 ||
        count > lengths[row]) {
        return 1;
    }
    int sum = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        sum += rows[row][i];
    }
    printf("%d\n", sum);
    return 0;
}

Validate the row before indexing its length entry.
